alignments.note: Expressed copula with its subject pronoun; the periphrastic auxiliary is what realizes this token.
`πλουτέω` rendered periphrastically *are become rich*; subject and copular auxiliaries ride inside the unit and rule 17 heads on the meaning-bearing *rich* rather than on the auxiliary *become*.
Ingressive aorist rendered *ye have come to reign*; subject and auxiliaries are rule 9 helpers and the head is the lexical *reign*.
Improper preposition rendered by the single English word *without*; rule 71 makes that word the head.
Governed genitive standing bare, the adverb having taken its own word (rule 42).
Emphatic particle rendered *yea*; the ASV places it before the conjunction, and rule 15 permits the reordering.
`ὄφελον` rendered by the frame *I would that*; the supplied subject and the complementizer belong to this token, which licenses the English clause, and the head is the lexical modal *would*.
Aorist with supplied subject and auxiliary, headed on the lexical *reign*.
Purpose conjunction realized by the word introducing its English clause (rule 40).
Compound verb with its modal auxiliary, headed on the verb word and never on the particle (rule 106).

The compound verb governs a bare dative and the ASV writes an English verb word of its own for it, so under rule 106's dative-government arm the preposition realizes the case government and rides with the governed pronoun, as ACT.4.1 `ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς` → *came* / *upon them* does. Reading *with* as the `συν-` preverb's own particle inside the verb's unit remains defensible.
